AFC.definition: any Competition where a Sprint is scheduled.

CC.definition: defined as a car which was designed and constructed in order to comply with the Regulations of the 2026 or subsequent Championships. No Competitor may sell or make available any such Current Car to any third party without the prior authorisation of the FIA.

DE.definition: defined as an event in which a Competitor participates purely for marketing or demonstration purposes.

DMS.definition: the FIA provided document management and exchange system used as the primary means of document exchange with Competitors during a Competition.

HC.definition: defined as a car which was designed and constructed in order to comply with the Regulations in force during the years preceding those referred in the definition of a Previous Car.

LTCS.definition: any track running session during which the classification of the session is determined based upon the time taken by a driver to complete a single lap. Lap Time Classified Sessions include, but are not limited to, free practice sessions, the sprint qualifying session and the qualifying session.

OMS.definition: the FIA o`icial messaging system that will be used as a means of real-time or near real-time communication to all Competitors during a Competition. Unless otherwise specifically defined, where in these Sporting FIA F1 Regulations where it is stated that a pre-determined message will be sent to all Competitors, or that all Competitors will be notified or informed of specific information during a competition, this will be done using the O`icial Messaging System.

PC.definition: defined as a car which was designed and constructed in order to comply with the Regulations of any of the 2022 - 2025 Championships. No Competitor may sell or make available any such Previous Car to any third party without the prior authorisation of the FIA.

PE.definition: defined as an event in which a Competitor participates purely for marketing or promotional purposes using a Current Car.

RNC.definition: components which have a limitation in numbers that can be used by each driver in a Competition during a Championship.

RP.definition: defined as a period of time during which, with the exception of the provisions of Article B9.4.1, team personnel who are associated in any way with the operation of the F1 Cars are not permitted within the confines of the circuit

SFC.definition: any Competition where a Race is scheduled and a Sprint is not scheduled.

TTCS.definition: any track running session during which the classification of the session is determined based upon the total time taken by a driver to complete a number of laps greater than one. Total Time Classified Sessions include, but are not limited to, the Sprint session and the Race session.

TCC.definition: defined as any track running time, not part of a Competition, in which a Competitor entered in the Championship participates (or in which a third party participates on behalf of a Competitor or a supplier of a homologated power unit), using a Current Car.

THC.definition: defined as any track running time, not part of a Competition, in which a Competitor entered in the Championship participates (or in which a third party participates on behalf of a Competitor or a supplier of a homologated power unit), using a Historic Car.

TMC.definition: defined as any track running time, not part of a Competition, in which a Competitor entered in the Championship participates (or in which a third party participates on behalf of a Competitor or a supplier of a homologated power unit), using a Mule Car.

Fast Lane.definition: The Pit Lane will be divided into two lanes, the lane closest to the pit wall will be designated the Fast Lane and may be no more than 3.5 metres wide.

Inner Lane.definition: The Pit Lane will be divided into two lanes, the lane closest to the garages will be designated the Inner lane.

Reserve Drivers.definition: tbc 2026 Regulations: General Regulatory Provisions 10 December 2025 A5 1 de l’Automobile Issue 01 GENERAL REGULATORY PROVISIONS
